Oddtoe is a character design service based in Melbourne and Los Angeles, building original characters for animation, games and comedy. One designer takes the brief from a first sketch to a finished spec sheet, in 2D, 2.5D or 3D, instead of a queue of freelancers passed between studios.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-icon" icon_size="30" delimiter_border_style="dotted" icon_fontawesome="fas fa-arrow-circle-down" show_icon="enable_icon" delim_line_color="#8224E31C" icon_color="#EEE6F6" icon_hover_color="#D4C9E0"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="35" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="35" screen_tablet_spacer_size="35" screen_mobile_spacer_size="35"][vc_single_image image="16126" img_size="large" alignment="center" css=""][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="35" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="35" screen_tablet_spacer_size="35" screen_mobile_spacer_size="35"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="The short version" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

What does a character design service actually do?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Oddtoe turns a brief, a script or a mood board into an original character ready for production, designing the look, personality and documentation together in 2D, 2.5D or 3D, so a studio, agency or games team can hand the character to other artists and get a consistent result.

Oddtoe is an experiential design and generative-AI animation studio based in Melbourne, creating projection, installation, and animated work for events, venues, and galleries.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="80" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="80" screen_tablet_spacer_size="80" screen_mobile_spacer_size="80"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Two words, two different jobs" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

Character designer or character design service, and does the difference matter?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

One character designer draws in their own style, at whatever pace they have free. A studio built for character design scopes the brief, documents the character properly and stays with the project through revisions, so the style does not drift between the first sketch and the hundredth frame.

The distinction matters most once a character has to survive more than one artist touching it. A single illustrator can hold a look in their head. The moment a second animator, a games team or an ad agency picks up the same character, someone needs a spec sheet: turnarounds, expressions, proportions, the details that keep a character on-model instead of drifting a little with every new hand.

It matters again on format. A character built for a static illustration is not automatically ready for a 3D model or an animated turn. Oddtoe designs with the eventual use in mind, so a character can move from 2D concept art to a 2.5D shaded pass to a full 3D model without a second designer reverse-engineering the first one's choices.

It cuts both ways: for a single static illustration in a style one artist already owns, a freelancer is often the better buy. See the character designer portfolio for the range of styles Oddtoe works in.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="60"][dfd_button button_text="Start a project" buttom_link_src="url:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.oddtoe.com%2Fcontact-oddtoe%2F|||" style="style_6" background="#8a8f6a" hover_background="#4e5041" border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;" hover_border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner el_class="dfd_col-tablet-12" width="1/4" offset="vc_col-lg-3 vc_col-md-2 vc_col-xs-1"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]

Questions & Answers

character design services

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14"][vc_tta_section title="How much does a character design service cost?" tab_id="1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

It depends on how many characters the brief needs, how many formats (2D, 2.5D or 3D) and how much documentation goes with each one. Oddtoe quotes per project after a short scoping conversation, so the number reflects your brief rather than a rate card you have to reverse-engineer.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="How do I choose a character design service?" tab_id="1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

Look at three things: whether the portfolio shows characters, not general illustration, whether one designer stays with the project through revisions, and whether they hand over proper spec sheets and turnarounds so other artists can draw the character consistently.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What formats does a character design service deliver?" tab_id="1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

For Oddtoe: 2D illustration, 2.5D (shaded to feel more dimensional) and full 3D models built for animation or games. Most briefs also get a spec sheet covering expressions, turnarounds and proportions, so the character stays consistent once other hands are drawing it.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can a character design service also animate the character?" tab_id="1685677784507-83427dcb-7a756fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

Yes, where the brief calls for it. Once a character is designed and documented, Oddtoe can take it into motion, including with generative AI as one technique in the pipeline. There is a fuller explanation on the generative AI animator page.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="I am a character designer looking for representation. Is this the right page?" tab_id="1786584255290-781b75e9-21a0"][vc_column_text css=""]

No. This page is for people who want a character designed. If you are an illustrator or character designer looking for an agent, Oddtoe keeps a separate guide to the animation agents and talent firms worth approaching. Start there instead.

What can a character design service create for you?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

2D illustration, 2.5D shaded designs, and full 3D models built for animation or games, each backed by a spec sheet covering expressions, turnarounds and proportions so the character stays consistent once other artists are drawing it.

Characters rarely arrive finished in one sitting. Oddtoe usually starts from a mood board or script and works through rough sketches before settling a final design, the same process behind the character designer portfolio.

Once a character is designed and documented, the next question is usually what it does next. Some go straight into motion — see the generative AI animator page for how Oddtoe treats AI as one technique in that pipeline. Others need a voice and a story first, which is where comedy and story writing comes in.

Characters that need to exist off the screen, as a costume, a prop or a physical build for an event, go through prop and 3D making instead, using the same design as its starting point.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-section-2"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="How to pick one" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

How do you choose a character design service?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Three tests. Does the portfolio show characters, not general illustration, will one designer stay with the project through revisions, and do they hand over proper spec sheets so other artists can draw the character consistently?

The portfolio test catches the most common mismatch. Plenty of illustrators can draw a striking single image; far fewer have designed a character built to be redrawn hundreds of times by other people without losing what made it work.

The continuity test matters because a character usually outlives the first design pass. If the designer who understood the brief is not the one answering revision notes in week four, you end up re-explaining the character to whoever inherited it.

The documentation test is the one people skip until it costs them. A character with no turnaround sheet looks fine in the first render and drifts in the second. I would rather hand over a spec sheet nobody needs than leave a studio guessing at an angle nobody drew.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" css=".vc_custom_1691550358421{background-color: #26161f !important;}" el_id="pat-article-1"][vc_column width="1/6"][/vc_column][vc_column width="4/6"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Why one designer beats a queue of them" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

One designer, one style, start to finish

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_column_text]

The case for hiring separate freelancers per asset is that it can be cheaper per image, and on a single static piece it often is. What that plan leaves out is what happens when the character has to work a second time: a different pose, a different medium, a sequel spot six months later. Somebody has to reverse-engineer the original designer's choices, and a look that took one afternoon to draw can take a week to match.

That is the part I try to remove up front. I take the brief, design the character in whichever formats the project actually needs, and build the documentation alongside it, not after somebody asks for it. A finished spec sheet means the next artist who touches the character, whether that is an animator, a games studio or a licensing partner, is working from the same reference I was.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_column_text]

The second thing a dedicated character design service buys is range across formats. A 2D illustration and a 3D model of the same character are different disciplines, and a character designed only for a still image often needs real rework before it can turn in three dimensions. Designing with the eventual use in mind from the first sketch avoids most of that rework.

None of that makes a full service the right answer every time. A single illustration in a style one artist already owns does not need a spec sheet built for a production it will never enter. The rule I use is simple: the more hands will touch the character, and the longer it has to last, the more the documentation is worth paying for up front.

Freelance illustrator or character design studio?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

The same character can be commissioned two ways. This is what changes between them.

CriterionFreelance illustratorCharacter design studio
Range of formatsWhatever that artist already draws in2D, 2.5D and 3D, designed together
DocumentationRarely includedSpec sheet: turnarounds, expressions, proportions
Style consistencyDepends on one person's availabilityDocumented so any artist can stay on-model
If the designer is unavailableThe project waitsOddtoe reassigns from the same brief and docs

So you need…

Character design services

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner el_class=”dfd_col-tablet-12″ width=”1/4″ offset=”vc_col-lg-3 vc_col-md-2 vc_col-xs-1″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner el_class=”dfd_col-tablet-12″ width=”1/2″ dfd_column_responsive_enable=”dfd-column-responsive-enable” offset=”vc_col-lg-6 vc_col-md-8 vc_col-xs-10″ css=”.vc_custom_1507277465182{padding-right: 0px !important;padding-left: 0px !important;}” responsive_styles=”padding_left_tablet:20|padding_right_tablet:20″][vc_column_text css=””]

Updated August 2026

[/vc_column_text]

[vc_column_text css=””]

Oddtoe is a character design service based in Melbourne and Los Angeles, building original characters for animation, games and comedy. One designer takes the brief from a first sketch to a finished spec sheet, in 2D, 2.5D or 3D, instead of a queue of freelancers passed between studios.

[/vc_column_text]

[vc_single_image image=”16126″ img_size=”large” alignment=”center” css=””]

The short version

What does a character design service actually do?

[vc_column_text css=””]

Oddtoe turns a brief, a script or a mood board into an original character ready for production, designing the look, personality and documentation together in 2D, 2.5D or 3D, so a studio, agency or games team can hand the character to other artists and get a consistent result.

Oddtoe is an experiential design and generative-AI animation studio based in Melbourne, creating projection, installation, and animated work for events, venues, and galleries.

[/vc_column_text]

Two words, two different jobs

Character designer or character design service, and does the difference matter?

[vc_column_text css=””]

One character designer draws in their own style, at whatever pace they have free. A studio built for character design scopes the brief, documents the character properly and stays with the project through revisions, so the style does not drift between the first sketch and the hundredth frame.

The distinction matters most once a character has to survive more than one artist touching it. A single illustrator can hold a look in their head. The moment a second animator, a games team or an ad agency picks up the same character, someone needs a spec sheet: turnarounds, expressions, proportions, the details that keep a character on-model instead of drifting a little with every new hand.

It matters again on format. A character built for a static illustration is not automatically ready for a 3D model or an animated turn. Oddtoe designs with the eventual use in mind, so a character can move from 2D concept art to a 2.5D shaded pass to a full 3D model without a second designer reverse-engineering the first one’s choices.

It cuts both ways: for a single static illustration in a style one artist already owns, a freelancer is often the better buy. See the character designer portfolio for the range of styles Oddtoe works in.

[/vc_column_text]

Start a projectStart a project
[/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner el_class=”dfd_col-tablet-12″ width=”1/4″ offset=”vc_col-lg-3 vc_col-md-2 vc_col-xs-1″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]
[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]
[vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” el_id=”pat-faq”][vc_column width=”1/4″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/2″]
[vc_column_text css=”” item_animation=”transition.fadeIn”]

Questions & Answers

character design services

[/vc_column_text]

[dfd_accordion style=”style-3″ active_section=”1″ font_size=”18″ tab_title_google_fonts=”yes” tab_title_custom_fonts=”font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal” icon_size=”14″][vc_tta_section title=”How much does a character design service cost?” tab_id=”1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

It depends on how many characters the brief needs, how many formats (2D, 2.5D or 3D) and how much documentation goes with each one. Oddtoe quotes per project after a short scoping conversation, so the number reflects your brief rather than a rate card you have to reverse-engineer.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”How do I choose a character design service?” tab_id=”1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

Look at three things: whether the portfolio shows characters, not general illustration, whether one designer stays with the project through revisions, and whether they hand over proper spec sheets and turnarounds so other artists can draw the character consistently.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”What formats does a character design service deliver?” tab_id=”1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

For Oddtoe: 2D illustration, 2.5D (shaded to feel more dimensional) and full 3D models built for animation or games. Most briefs also get a spec sheet covering expressions, turnarounds and proportions, so the character stays consistent once other hands are drawing it.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”Can a character design service also animate the character?” tab_id=”1685677784507-83427dcb-7a756fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

Yes, where the brief calls for it. Once a character is designed and documented, Oddtoe can take it into motion, including with generative AI as one technique in the pipeline. There is a fuller explanation on the generative AI animator page.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”I am a character designer looking for representation. Is this the right page?” tab_id=”1786584255290-781b75e9-21a0″][vc_column_text css=””]

No. This page is for people who want a character designed. If you are an illustrator or character designer looking for an agent, Oddtoe keeps a separate guide to the animation agents and talent firms worth approaching. Start there instead.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/dfd_accordion][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html]

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″]

What actually gets made

What can a character design service create for you?

[vc_column_text css=””]

2D illustration, 2.5D shaded designs, and full 3D models built for animation or games, each backed by a spec sheet covering expressions, turnarounds and proportions so the character stays consistent once other artists are drawing it.

Characters rarely arrive finished in one sitting. Oddtoe usually starts from a mood board or script and works through rough sketches before settling a final design, the same process behind the character designer portfolio.

Once a character is designed and documented, the next question is usually what it does next. Some go straight into motion — see the generative AI animator page for how Oddtoe treats AI as one technique in that pipeline. Others need a voice and a story first, which is where comedy and story writing comes in.

Characters that need to exist off the screen, as a costume, a prop or a physical build for an event, go through prop and 3D making instead, using the same design as its starting point.

[/vc_column_text]

[/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column]
[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]

[vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” dfd_row_config=”full_width_content_paddings” el_id=”pat-section-2″][vc_column]
[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″]

How to pick one

How do you choose a character design service?

[vc_column_text css=””]

Three tests. Does the portfolio show characters, not general illustration, will one designer stay with the project through revisions, and do they hand over proper spec sheets so other artists can draw the character consistently?

The portfolio test catches the most common mismatch. Plenty of illustrators can draw a striking single image; far fewer have designed a character built to be redrawn hundreds of times by other people without losing what made it work.

The continuity test matters because a character usually outlives the first design pass. If the designer who understood the brief is not the one answering revision notes in week four, you end up re-explaining the character to whoever inherited it.

The documentation test is the one people skip until it costs them. A character with no turnaround sheet looks fine in the first render and drifts in the second. I would rather hand over a spec sheet nobody needs than leave a studio guessing at an angle nobody drew.

[/vc_column_text]

[/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column]
[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]
[vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” css=”.vc_custom_1691550358421{background-color: #26161f !important;}” el_id=”pat-article-1″][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”4/6″]

Why one designer beats a queue of them

One designer, one style, start to finish

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_column_text]

The case for hiring separate freelancers per asset is that it can be cheaper per image, and on a single static piece it often is. What that plan leaves out is what happens when the character has to work a second time: a different pose, a different medium, a sequel spot six months later. Somebody has to reverse-engineer the original designer’s choices, and a look that took one afternoon to draw can take a week to match.

That is the part I try to remove up front. I take the brief, design the character in whichever formats the project actually needs, and build the documentation alongside it, not after somebody asks for it. A finished spec sheet means the next artist who touches the character, whether that is an animator, a games studio or a licensing partner, is working from the same reference I was.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_column_text]

The second thing a dedicated character design service buys is range across formats. A 2D illustration and a 3D model of the same character are different disciplines, and a character designed only for a still image often needs real rework before it can turn in three dimensions. Designing with the eventual use in mind from the first sketch avoids most of that rework.

None of that makes a full service the right answer every time. A single illustration in a style one artist already owns does not need a spec sheet built for a production it will never enter. The rule I use is simple: the more hands will touch the character, and the longer it has to last, the more the documentation is worth paying for up front.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

Freelance illustrator or character design studio?

[vc_column_text css=””]

The same character can be commissioned two ways. This is what changes between them.
